behavior: Diurnal, arboreal, and nonmigratory. Usually forages alone or in pairs and may join small flocks with other orioles, taking insects, fruit, and nectar; its straight bill can pry pulp from firm fruit. Vocalizations include melodious rising-and-falling whistles and chattering calls.
field_marks: Bright orange head, back, and underparts, often yellower on the body
Restricted black lores and neatly defined black throat bib
Dark wings with two bold white wing bars and whitish primary edges
Long, straight, sharply pointed black bill with a blue-gray lower base
Fairly long, dark tail; dark eyes and grayish legs
Female duller yellow-orange with an olive-washed mantle and browner tail
habitat: Open tropical woodland, forest edge, second growth, scrub, and savanna, often near fresh water; also uses semi-open disturbed or agricultural habitat with hedges and scattered trees.
